**Date:** October 27, 2026  

**To:**  
The Editors-in-Chief  
*Computers & Geosciences*  
Elsevier Science  

**Subject:** Submission of original research paper titled *"A Reproducible Computational Framework for Decoupled Wildfire Ignition and Propagation Benchmarking in the Gran Chaco (2018–2025)"*  

Dear Editors-in-Chief,

Please find enclosed our original research manuscript entitled **"A Reproducible Computational Framework for Decoupled Wildfire Ignition and Propagation Benchmarking in the Gran Chaco (2018–2025): D2 Targets, M3/M2 Inference and an Open Benchmark Against Canadian FWI and INPE"**, which we submit for consideration as a **Research Paper** in *Computers & Geosciences*.

### Motivation and Core Scientific Novelty
Operational wildfire forecasting in geoscience machine learning frequently suffers from two pervasive methodological pathologies:
1. **Spatial Shortcut Learning:** When models include autoregressive spatial lags without isolating causal mechanisms, gradient-boosted ensembles learn trivial spatial persistence heuristics (*"fire will persist where thermal anomalies already exist"*), resulting in severe false confidence while remaining incapable of anticipating new, spontaneous, or anthropic primary ignitions.
2. **Failure of Canonical Boreal Indices in the Subtropics:** Widely deployed operational frameworks—such as the Canadian Forest Fire Weather Index (FWI) used by EFFIS/GWIS and the CPTEC/INPE Risco de Fogo—consistently fail or invert hazard rankings in water-limited subtropical biomes (e.g., the South American Gran Chaco), where vapor pressure deficit ($VPD$) and non-linear fuel-curing dynamics govern fire risk.

To address these challenges, we introduce `Incendios_PY`, an open-source computational framework for reproducible decoupled wildfire modelling across **$400,006$ $1\text{-km}^2$ grid cells** over an 8-year homogeneous multi-annual observation baseline (2018–2025). This horizon is strictly anchored to the dual-sensor VIIRS 375m constellation (Suomi-NPP and NOAA-20 in continuous orbital tandem), systematically eliminating observational effort bias and ensuring uniform temporal sampling across all modeling phases. We analytically decouple the operational task into two distinct models: (i) **Multiscale Socio-Ecological Hybrid Ignition** ($\mathcal{M}_3$), guided by physics-based monotonic constraints, ecotone edge gradients, and static anthropogenic priors at 10-km and 25-km scales; and (ii) **Tactical Propagation**, driven by a causal spatial contagion kernel at lag $t-1$.

### Why this Manuscript Fits *Computers & Geosciences*
Our work sits precisely at the convergence of **Computer Science Applications** and **Earth and Planetary Sciences**. The contribution is a reusable protocol and benchmark, not a new boosting algorithm: D2 target construction, M3/M2 inference, and a reproducible evaluation harness are the computational core.

* **High-Performance Zero-Copy Computational Pipeline:** By integrating Apache Arrow, DuckDB, and Polars, our computational engine processes the entire national territory ($400,006\text{ km}^2$) in **~$1.57$ seconds** on a standard ARM64 machine (~$2.18\text{ GB}$ peak RAM), demonstrating that national early-warning systems do not require prohibitive cloud infrastructure.
* **Physics-Guided Machine Learning (PGML):** We enforce structural monotonic constraints within LightGBM ($+1$ for atmospheric dryness and wind pressure, $-1$ for antecedent rainfall and distance), mathematically preventing counterintuitive artifacts.
* **Spatial and Temporal Control:** We use the **D2 target definition** (no t-1 fire within 25 km; no same-cell fire in 10 days) and multi-year out-of-time test partitions (2024–2025). We also implement a **50-km spatial block holdout with a 20-km buffer**; a reproducible semivariogram remains pending. Priors are causal (monthly cutoff, rolling 3-year window).
* **Software Engineering and Reproducibility Standards:** The framework is packaged with a complete automated test suite of **76 unit tests** (`tests/`) running in $\approx 1\text{ minute}$, verifying algebraic invariants, physical monotonicity, conformal coverage, and spatial KD-Tree queries. All code and workflows are versioned from raw ingestion (`scripts/00_...`) to publication-ready outputs (`scripts/24_...`) under the permissive MIT License.
* **Quantitative International Benchmarking:** In retrospective temporal testing over $1,813,966$ D2 cell-days during 2024–2025, our hybrid ignition layer $\mathcal{M}_3$ achieves a ROC-AUC of **$0.8021$** in the Gran Chaco and **$0.7534$** in the Oriental Region, versus **$0.5173$ / $0.5564$** for the full Canadian FWI and **$0.5389$ / $0.4990$** for the INPE. Case-control $F_{0.5}$ precision is $32.82\text{ \%}$ / $30.13\text{ \%}$; after correction to population prevalence (~0.015 % / 0.041 %), operational precision is $0.082\text{ \%}$ / $0.198\text{ \%}$. Tactical propagation achieves ROC-AUC **$0.9039$** (Chaco) and population precision $9.67\text{ \%}$. The 2023 validation selected M3 for temporal nowcasting and M2 as the operational fallback; M1 was rejected as a fallback. These corrected metrics are the honest operational benchmark.
